hooks.text: This tiny dwarf galaxy is having a violent growth spurt.
Why is this small galaxy glowing like a neon sign?
This dwarf galaxy is outshining the giants around it.

title: The Galaxy Having a Growth Spurt
description: NGC 4449 is a dwarf irregular galaxy undergoing an intense starburst triggered by gravitational interactions with its neighbors.

beats.text: This tiny dwarf galaxy is having a violent growth spurt.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope high resolution image of NGC 4449, 2011

beats.text: Astronomer William Herschel spotted NGC 4449 and saw a mess.
beats.visual: Portrait of astronomer William Herschel, painting by John Russell

beats.text: It has no spiral arms, just a chaotic, irregular shape.
beats.visual: Wide view of NGC 4449 showing irregular structure and scattered stars

beats.text: But telescopes found vibrant pink clouds of glowing gas.
beats.visual: Hubble image detail of pink hydrogen gas regions in NGC 4449

beats.text: These clouds are intense nurseries creating massive waves of stars.
beats.visual: Artist concept of new stars forming inside dense hydrogen gas clouds

beats.text: They even spotted huge clusters of young, blue-white stars.
beats.visual: Hubble image focusing on young blue-white star clusters in NGC 4449

beats.text: The clue to this chaos was hiding in the neighbors.
beats.visual: Star map of the constellation Canes Venatici showing the location of NGC 4449

beats.text: Nearby galaxies pulled on it in a cosmic interaction.
beats.visual: Diagram illustrating gravitational interaction and tidal forces between two galaxies

beats.text: And this gravitational tug-of-war with neighbor galaxies is why.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope wide field image of NGC 4449, 2011

better_than_last: Integrated reviewer feedback for the hook and loop, modifying the hook to exactly 10 words and correcting the emphasis in beat 2 to match the spoken text.
